newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS TAKES FIRST SET 6-2 IN AUSTRALIA FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS TAKES FIRST SET 6-2 IN AUSTRALIA FINAL.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras won the opening set 6-2 against Spain's Carlos Moya in the final of the Australian Open tennis tournament on Sunday.
Both players started strongly, producing aces to win their opening service games comfortably before Sampras broke his unseeded opponent's serve in the fourth game to take a 3-1 lead.
On a sunny day at Melbourne Park, Sampras broke Moya again in the eighth game to take the set in just 23 minutes. Sampras served powerfully and managed to dominate Moya from the net.
Sampras, who won in Melbourne in 1994 and was runner-up the following year, is aiming for his ninth Grand Slam title.
Sampras won the second set 6-3, maintaining his momentum from the opening set.
He held his own serve and then broke Moya for a 2-0 lead. The American right-hander pounced on Moya's shallow second serves, charging to the net to set up simple volley winners.
The Spaniard valiantly fought back, grabbing a break of his own in the third game of the set and levelled the score at 2-2 when he held serve.
Moya had a chance to break Sampras again in the seventh game but was unable to convert a break point, spraying his backhand shot wide.
Sampras took a 5-3 lead when he broke Moya with a forehand cross-court winner and then served out to take the set in 26 minutes.
Sampras, 25, clinched his ninth Grand Slam title when he took the third set 6-3, ending the match after just 87 minutes.

Moya, ranked 25th in the world, rarely showed the game which he used in upset victories over defending champion Boris Becker in the opening round and world number two Michael chang in the semi-finals.
Sampras outclassed his rival in every facet of the game, smashing winners from the baseline, placing deft drop shots and stunning Moya with his sharp net play.

The American broke the 20-year-old's serve early in the third set to lead 3-1 and rattled off three aces in the eighth game to go 5-3 up. He built up a 0-40 lead against Moya's serve in the next game and clinched the championship on the next point.
